metadata.title: Is now the time to buy software stocks?

content.text:
Opening Bid Host Brooke DiPalma is joined by the panel of Prime Capital Financial chief investment officer Will McGough, Slatestone Wealth chief market strategist Kenny Polcari, and F.L. Putnam Investment Management co-chief market strategist & portfolio manager Ellen Hazen to weigh whether now is the time to buy into software stocks.
The best performing S&P 500 stocks this week could be a bullish signal for the battered software sector. Salesforce, Crowdstrike, Synopsys, ServiceNow and Palo Alto, all in the top 10, strong earnings from Salesforce and Crowdstrike really provided a counter to the fears of AI destroying the software business. Plus, as these AI models get stronger, cyber security stocks continue to perform well. So with that in mind, my question of the day is, is now the time for investors to get into software? Let's take it to the panel here. I do want to start with Will because you said that you never really bought into this narrative of the SASpocalypse even to begin with.
Right, as a portfolio team, we sat around when all the news was headding in Q1. And just think about this simplistically, is Salesforce really going to be taken over by a bunch of Fortune 500 companies using AI to rewrite Salesforce? Naively the answer is no. And so what we're actually seeing right now while software has gotten dinged so much is a real-time rerating of the growth versus value definitions and we really work with our clients and advisors to shed those labels. Growth and value can mean a lot of different things to a lot of different people. And so it's really having prudent exposure to the whole tech stack, whether it's software or hardware, AI or not. and also finding allocations away from that to diversify the risks when something will go wrong down the road, you have appropriate diversification for that.
Kenny, are the worst days for Salesforce behind us now?
I I think so. I mean, I I think so. and look what happened yesterday. We saw a massive move in Salesforce. I think we saw that whole sector and to your point, you mentioned cyber security, right? That's all part of that stack. And so, I think it's a great opportunity. If you're not in, you should be getting in. It's a great time to get in because it's been so beaten up. But if you're in, if you've already been in and you've kind of ridden it down, now's also a good time to add to those positions on some of those key names. and you saw how they all reacted yesterday. They exploded higher. They didn't just move higher. They exploded higher. And so yes, I think you have to be in it. and to Will's point, you know, it's a matter of about being in across the board, not just being in one part of the tech stack, but kind of across the board in the tech stack.
Allen, you say that you should be rotating out of hardware right now into software? Can you walk us through that strategy there?
Yeah, the hardware names have done really, really well this year, especially, uh, most year to date, and the software names have taken it on the chin as you know, because of the perceived SASpocalypse. But I think, uh, that the point is very true that you need to look at the details, not just paint them with a broad brush. Are people really going to wipe out Salesforce? Are they really going to yank out Palo Alto networks and just they're on cyber security? I don't think so. And so it has always made much more sense to be much more careful and detailed about that. We always look at earnings estimates and earnings estimates for a company like Salesforce have been going up for two years. And of course up a lot more yesterday after the results. But what we're seeing is that the stocks are reacting rationally in a way that in the first half of the year, they really were not. And so software had become oversold technically, while hardware was overbought technically. And again, if we are correct that the trillion dollars may not be able to be spent next year because of permitting labor, other constraints, then hardware may face a tough time of it as those uh revenues get pushed out a little bit, whereas software is certainly uh cheap stocks, high quality businesses and you just need to be really careful and thoughtful about which ones you want to own.
Kenny, Take two is one of the top trending tickers on our site today. Everyone seems to be focused on that Grand Theft Auto 6. Are you a buyer there?
I don't do Grand Theft Auto. I'm 65 years old. I haven't played a a video game. I can't remember when. So, again, I'm probably not the right person to talk about take two because it's not in my wheelhouse.
